edit.description: `append` (~:288) relativizes an `InstructionsLoaded` identity against `log_path(workspace_dir).parent().and_then(Path::parent)` — the primary checkout's root, because `log_path` redirects a linked worktree's log there. A file inside the worktree is not under the primary root, so `strip_prefix` fails and the identity stays absolute. Relativize against the root the tap ran from (`workspace_dir.parent()`) instead; `log_path`'s own primary-checkout redirection is correct and stays.

`log_path_resolves_linked_worktree_to_primary_checkout` (~:258) appends a `ToolUse` record, which carries no path to relativize, so the worktree case has never exercised the rewrite. Add the `InstructionsLoaded` half over the same real `git worktree add` fixture: a rule path inside the worktree records the repo-relative id one worktree shares with the primary, with the absolute original in `raw_path`.

summary: A tap record appended from a linked worktree keeps an absolute identity, so each worktree gets its own id for one rule and the read-time join to lock members breaks.

tests.asserts: an `InstructionsLoaded` append from a real linked worktree records the same repo-relative identity a primary-checkout append records, and `raw_path` keeps the absolute original

acceptance: `cargo test --test tap` green with the new worktree case, which fails on the pre-fix tree (the identity reads absolute); `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
notes: "The reader joins raw events to members through the lock's own declarations" is what an absolute identity breaks — one rule reads as N members, one per worktree. 0062's new trigger/parent paths take the same relativization; the spec-delta tick that derives 0062 widens this entry rather than filing a sibling. Confirmed by reading src/tap.rs, not run. scoped at b95d5e8f
